## From a script to a Snakefile

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em; margin-bottom: 0.4em;"}
Same intent — *align each FASTQ, call variants per sample, merge into a cohort VCF*. The script hard-codes the loop; the Snakefile **declares the dependencies** and lets Snakemake build the DAG.
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #7f8c8d; margin: 0 0 0.3em;"><i class="mdi mdi-script-text-outline"></i>&nbsp; Bash-style pseudo-script</h4>

```{.bash style="font-size: 0.82em;"}
for S in A B C; do
  bwa mem ref fq/$S.fq.gz \
    | samtools sort -o bam/$S.bam
  gatk HaplotypeCaller \
    -I bam/$S.bam -O vcf/$S.vcf
done

bcftools merge \
  vcf/A.vcf vcf/B.vcf vcf/C.vcf \
  > vcf/cohort.vcf
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
Linear · no parallelism · re-runs everything · no provenance.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #208F6E; margin: 0 0 0.3em;"><i class="mdi mdi-snake"></i>&nbsp; Snakefile</h4>

```{.snakemake style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
SAMPLES = ["A", "B", "C"]

rule all:
    input: "vcf/cohort.vcf"

rule align:
    input:  "fq/{s}.fq.gz"
    output: "bam/{s}.bam"
    shell:  "bwa mem ref {input} | samtools sort -o {output}"

rule call:
    input:  "bam/{s}.bam"
    output: "vcf/{s}.vcf"
    shell:  "gatk HaplotypeCaller -I {input} -O {output}"

rule merge:
    input:  expand("vcf/{s}.vcf", s=SAMPLES)
    output: "vcf/cohort.vcf"
    shell:  "bcftools merge {input} > {output}"
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; color: #208F6E; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
Parallel by default · resumable · per-rule env · DAG up-front.
:::
:::
:::

## A rule — zoom in

::: {style="font-size: 0.95em; margin-bottom: 0.4em;"}
A **pipeline is organised as a list of rules**. Each rule is **one step** — *e.g.* align FASTQs, call variants, build a plot — declared by its inputs, outputs and how to produce one from the other.
:::

::: {.four-ideas}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="25%"}
::: {.idea-card}
<i class="mdi mdi-asterisk idea-icon"></i>
<div class="big-label">Wildcards</div>
<div class="sub-label">inferred from targets</div>
:::
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
::: {.idea-card}
<i class="mdi mdi-tune idea-icon"></i>
<div class="big-label">Params</div>
<div class="sub-label">non-file config</div>
:::
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
::: {.idea-card}
<i class="mdi mdi-cpu-64-bit idea-icon"></i>
<div class="big-label">Resources</div>
<div class="sub-label">cpu · mem · runtime</div>
:::
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
::: {.idea-card}
<i class="mdi mdi-package-variant idea-icon"></i>
<div class="big-label">Env per rule</div>
<div class="sub-label">conda · container · module</div>
:::
:::
:::
:::

```{.snakemake}
rule align:
    input:   "fastq/{sample}.fq.gz"          # wildcards: {sample}
    output:  "bam/{sample}.bam"
    log:     "logs/{sample}.log"
    params:  min_mapq = 30                   # → {params.min_mapq}
    threads: 8
    resources: mem_mb=16_000, runtime=120    # SLURM-aware
    conda:   "envs/bwa.yaml"                 # or container: / envmodules:
    shell:
        "bwa mem -t {threads} ref {input} | "
        "samtools view -q {params.min_mapq} -b - | "
        "samtools sort -o {output} 2> {log}"
```

## Wildcards → DAG → dry-run

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
You request **an output file** → Snakemake recurses back through rules until it hits files that exist. The DAG is built **statically**.

```bash
snakemake results.txt --dry-run
snakemake --rulegraph | dot -Tsvg > rules.svg
```

## Conditional execution — checkpoints

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
**Pattern.** Step 1 produces an **actionable verdict** (a table, a pass/fail list). Step 2 must **only run on the survivors** — the DAG branches that should never execute are pruned at runtime.

```{.snakemake style="font-size: 0.66em;"}
# upstream — produce per-cell counts
rule count_cell:
    input:  "bam/{cell}.bam"
    output: "counts/{cell}.tsv"

# checkpoint — score every cell, write a verdict table
checkpoint filter_cells:
    input:  expand("counts/{cell}.tsv", cell=ALL_CELLS)
    output: "qc/verdict.tsv"           # columns: cell, keep(bool)
    script: "scripts/qc_filter.py"

# per surviving cell (normal rule)
rule call_sv:
    input:  "counts/{cell}.tsv"
    output: "sv/{cell}.calls.tsv"

# input function — .get() blocks on the checkpoint, then
# the DAG is re-evaluated with only the cells we keep
def passing(wildcards):
    verdict = checkpoints.filter_cells.get().output[0]
    kept = pd.read_table(verdict).query("keep").cell
    return expand("sv/{cell}.calls.tsv", cell=kept)

rule collect:                          # ◀ consumes the function
    input:  passing
    output: "sv/all_calls.tsv"
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.72em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-alert" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Replaces legacy `dynamic()` — removed in v8.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
::: {style="font-size: 0.74em; color: #34495E; text-align: center; margin: 0 0 0.4em; line-height: 1.4;"}
The checkpoint emits the verdict; the input function then **prunes** the per-cell edges — they are discovered at runtime, not declared up-front.
:::

```{mermaid}
%%| eval: true
%%| echo: false
%%| fig-align: center
flowchart TD
  C1["count cell_1"] --> CP
  C2["count cell_2"] --> CP
  C3["count cell_3"] --> CP
  C4["count cell_4"] --> CP
  C5["count cell_5"] --> CP
  CP["checkpoint<br/>filter_cells"]
  CP --> SV1["call_sv cell_1 ✓"]
  CP -. skipped .-> X2["cell_2 ✗"]
  CP --> SV3["call_sv cell_3 ✓"]
  CP -. skipped .-> X4["cell_4 ✗"]
  CP --> SV5["call_sv cell_5 ✓"]
  SV1 --> RA["collect"]
  SV3 --> RA
  SV5 --> RA
  classDef cp fill:#fef5e7,stroke:#E67E22,color:#6e3906,stroke-width:2px;
  classDef pass fill:#e8f5f0,stroke:#208F6E,color:#0f3a30;
  classDef fail fill:#fdecea,stroke:#C0392B,color:#922b21,stroke-dasharray: 4 3;
  classDef src fill:#eef3f7,stroke:#7f8c8d,color:#34495E;
  classDef goal fill:#f4ecf7,stroke:#8E44AD,color:#4a235a;
  class CP cp
  class SV1,SV3,SV5 pass
  class X2,X4 fail
  class C1,C2,C3,C4,C5 src
  class RA goal
```
:::
:::

## Reproducibility & provenance

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #208F6E;"><i class="mdi mdi-anvil"></i>&nbsp; Per-rule software · 3 options</h4>

```{.snakemake style="font-size: 0.78em;"}
rule call_snvs:
    conda:      "envs/gatk.yaml"
    container:  "docker://.../gatk:4.5"
    envmodules: "GATK/4.5"
    shell: "gatk HaplotypeCaller ..."
```

::: {style="white-space: nowrap; font-size: 0.92em;"}
Pick one, or compose: `--sdm conda apptainer`
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #208F6E;"><i class="mdi mdi-file-document"></i>&nbsp; Reports — auto since 9.1</h4>

```{.snakemake style="font-size: 0.68em;"}
rule plot_qc:
    output: report(
        "plots/{s}.svg",
        caption="report/qc.rst",     # ◀ method text
        category="QC",               # ◀ top-level tab
        subcategory="Per cell",      # ◀ nested group
        labels={"sample": "{s}"},    # ◀ searchable table
        patterns=["{name}.svg"],     # ◀ dir → many files
    )
    script: "scripts/plot_qc.py"
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.68em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.2em;"}
`snakemake --report report.html --report-after-run` (v9.1) — auto, no second run.
:::
:::
:::

## Conda + container — two ways to combine

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #208F6E; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-layers-triple"></i>&nbsp; Ad hoc — conda *inside* a global container</h4>

A **global** `container:` statement (top of the Snakefile) + per-rule `conda:` → Snakemake enters the container, **then builds the env inside it**:

```{.snakemake style="font-size: 0.7em;"}
# top of the Snakefile (global, not per-rule)
container: "docker://condaforge/miniforge3"

rule call_snvs:
    conda: "envs/gatk.yaml"
    shell: "gatk HaplotypeCaller ..."
```

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.74em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
Pinned OS **and** pinned packages, no bespoke image to build. Env hash includes the image URL.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #208F6E; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-cube-send"></i>&nbsp; Bake — `--containerize` all envs into one image</h4>

```bash
snakemake --containerize > Dockerfile
docker build -t myorg/mc:2.5.0 .
```

Then pin the workflow to that prebuilt image:

```{.snakemake style="font-size: 0.7em;"}
# top of the Snakefile
containerized: "docker://myorg/mc:2.5.0"

rule call_snvs:
    conda: "envs/gatk.yaml"   # baked in
    shell: "gatk HaplotypeCaller ..."
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.74em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
One image holds **all** envs → no per-node solves; ship to CI / air-gapped HPC; reproducible to the byte.
:::
:::
:::

## Driving Snakemake from Python — the API

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
Since v8 the engine is **importable** — no `subprocess`, no CLI string. Snakemake becomes a **library you embed in a larger stack** (a service, a watcher, a Nextflow-style orchestrator, a notebook):

```{.python style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
from snakemake.api import (
    SnakemakeApi, OutputSettings, ResourceSettings,
    ConfigSettings, DeploymentSettings, DeploymentMethod,
    DefaultResources, DAGSettings, ExecutionSettings,
)

with SnakemakeApi(OutputSettings(dryrun=False)) as api:
    wf = api.workflow(
        resource_settings=ResourceSettings(
            nodes=150,
            default_resources=DefaultResources(["mem_mb=500"]),
        ),
        config_settings=ConfigSettings(config={"samples": new_run}),
        deployment_settings=DeploymentSettings(
            deployment_method={DeploymentMethod.CONDA,
                               DeploymentMethod.APPTAINER},
        ),
        snakefile=PIPELINE / "workflow" / "Snakefile",
        workdir=PIPELINE,
    )
    dag = wf.dag(dag_settings=DAGSettings(force_incomplete=True))
    dag.execute_workflow(executor="slurm", ...)   # SLURM settings
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<div style="background: #e8f5f0; border-left: 4px solid #208F6E; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.9em 1em; font-size: 0.84em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-engine-outline" style="color: #208F6E; font-size: 1.3em;"></i>

**Snakemake as an engine**

- **watcher** — auto-launch on new data landing
- **web service / REST** — run pipelines on request
- **orchestrator step** — a node inside a bigger DAG
- **notebook** — drive runs interactively, inspect the DAG

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em; margin-top: 0.5em; color: #34495E;"}
The CLI is just a thin wrapper over these `*Settings` objects — anything the CLI does, you can do programmatically.
:::
</div>
:::
:::

## Monolith → plugin framework

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

<h3 style="color: #8E44AD;"><i class="mdi mdi-package-variant-closed"></i>&nbsp; v7 (monolith)</h3>

All executors, all remote-storage backends, all software-deployment options shipped in **one package**.

```bash
snakemake --use-conda \
          --use-singularity \
          --cluster "sbatch ..."
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<h3 style="color: #8E44AD;"><i class="mdi mdi-puzzle"></i>&nbsp; v8 / v9 (plugins)</h3>

Engine + **5 plugin types**, each pip-installable:

- <i class="mdi mdi-server"></i>&nbsp; **Executor** — slurm, k8s, googlebatch …
- <i class="mdi mdi-database"></i>&nbsp; **Storage** — fs, s3, gcs, zenodo …
- <i class="mdi mdi-text-box"></i>&nbsp; **Logger** — snkmt …
- <i class="mdi mdi-file-document"></i>&nbsp; **Report** — rocrate, nanopub …
- <i class="mdi mdi-clock-fast"></i>&nbsp; **Scheduler** — greedy, ilp, milp
:::
:::

```bash
pip install snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm
snakemake --executor slurm --jobs 100 \
```

## Compose storage *and* compute

::: {style="font-size: 0.88em; margin-bottom: 0.4em;"}
One workflow, **many backends** — each rule's inputs/outputs can sit on a different storage, and each rule can run on a different executor.
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #8E44AD; margin: 0 0 0.3em;"><i class="mdi mdi-database"></i>&nbsp; Storage — S3 + Zenodo + local + GCS</h4>

```{.snakemake style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
storage s3_aws:   provider="s3"
storage refs_zen: provider="zenodo", doi="10.5281/zenodo.1234567"
storage out_gcs:  provider="gcs",    project="korbel-out"

rule align:
    input:
        reads = storage.s3_aws("s3://run42/{s}.fq.gz"),  # S3
        ref   = storage.refs_zen("hg38.fa"),              # Zenodo
        bed   = "panels/exome.bed",                       # local fs
    output:
        storage.out_gcs("gs://korbel-out/{s}.bam"),       # GCS
    shell:
        "bwa mem {input.ref} {input.reads} "
        "| samtools sort -o {output}"
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.74em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
Plugins: `fs` · `s3` · `gcs` · `azure` · `http` · `ftp` · `zenodo` · `xrootd` …
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #8E44AD; margin: 0 0 0.3em;"><i class="mdi mdi-server-network"></i>&nbsp; Compute — SLURM + K8s + local</h4>

```{.yaml filename="profile/config.yaml" style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
executor: slurm        # default: HPC
jobs: 200

set-resources:         # per-rule overrides
  bwa_align:      { executor: slurm,      mem_mb: 16000 }
  call_variants:  { executor: slurm,      mem_mb: 32000 }
  run_deepvar:    { executor: kubernetes }   # GPU pool
  summary_html:   { executor: local      }   # head node
```

```{.bash style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
pip install snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm \
            snakemake-executor-plugin-kubernetes
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.74em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
Executors: `slurm` · `kubernetes` · `googlebatch` · `azure-batch` · `lsf` · `htcondor` · `flux` · `local` …
:::
:::
:::

## Software deployment — one flag

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
<h4 style="color: #8E44AD; margin-top: 0;">v7 — many flags</h4>
```bash
--use-conda
--use-singularity
--use-envmodules
--conda-frontend mamba
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
<h4 style="color: #8E44AD; margin-top: 0;">v8 / v9 — one flag</h4>
```bash
--sdm conda         # conda env per rule
--sdm apptainer     # Apptainer/Singularity
--sdm env-modules   # HPC env-modules (EESSI…)
--sdm conda apptainer    # compose
```
:::
:::

::: {style="margin-top: 1em;"}
**Per-rule directives — all three are supported simultaneously:**
:::

```{.snakemake}
rule align:
    conda:      "envs/bwa.yaml"                  # ◀ conda
    container:  "docker://biocontainers/bwa:0.7.17"  # ◀ container
    envmodules: "BWA/0.7.17", "SAMtools/1.18"    # ◀ env-modules
    shell: "bwa mem ..."
```

::: {style="margin-top: 0.6em; font-size: 0.82em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-information" style="color: #8E44AD;"></i>&nbsp; `--conda-frontend mamba` **removed** ([PR #3121](https://github.com/snakemake/snakemake/pull/3121)) — `libmamba` is the default solver since Conda 23.10 · Pixi backend on the roadmap.
:::

## Plugin catalog · scheduler — `firstfit`

**What.** Replaces the default **ILP** scheduler with a **first-fit-decreasing** heuristic — faster scheduling on workflows with thousands of jobs (ILP can stall on the DAG-search step).

```bash
pip install snakemake-scheduler-plugin-firstfit
snakemake --scheduler firstfit --jobs 5000
```

::: {style="margin-top: 0.6em; padding: 0.55em 0.9em; background: #f4ecf7; border-left: 4px solid #8E44AD; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.82em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-information"></i>&nbsp; Trade-off: faster scheduling decisions, **less globally optimal** packing than ILP. Worth it once the ILP overhead dominates the actual job runtime.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
[plugins/scheduler/firstfit](https://snakemake.github.io/snakemake-plugin-catalog/plugins/scheduler/firstfit.html)
:::

## Plugin catalog · report — RO-Crate / nanopub

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
Report plugins **auto-activate when installed** — there is **no `--report-plugin` flag**. The standard `--report` invocation triggers whatever report plugins are on the Python path.

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.4em; padding: 0.4em 0.7em; background: #fef5e7; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px;"}

```bash
pip install snakemake-report-plugin-rocrate snakemake-report-plugin-nanopub
snakemake --report report.html         # the installed plugins extend the output
```

Emits a **Workflow-Run RO-Crate** (Leo et al. PLOS ONE 2024) — JSON-LD bundle with the workflow, every input/output, software versions, run metadata.

Auto-publishes a **nanopublication** (FAIR semantic claim) after every successful run — workflow, configuration, dataset, report → linked nodes in the knowledge graph.

Route events into your monitoring stack — a **message bus** (STOMP/AMQP) or a **metrics endpoint** (Prometheus / Grafana) — to watch many runs across the cluster from one place.

## Stability & backward-compatibility — issues to watch

::: {style="font-size: 0.92em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
The engine moves faster than user pipelines. Same Snakefile, different minor → sometimes different behaviour.
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #C0392B; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-close-circle"></i>&nbsp; Removed / renamed</h4>

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em;"}
- `dynamic()` outputs → **checkpoints**
- `version:` directive → `conda:` / `container:`
- `subworkflow:` → `module:` + `use rule …`
- `from snakemake.remote.*` → `storage` directive
- v7 profiles silently broken on v8 (removed flags)
:::

<div style="margin-top: 0.5em; padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #fdecea; border-left: 4px solid #C0392B; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.8em;">
<b>CI / containers</b> — list every plugin explicitly (`snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm`, …) or `--executor slurm` exits with *plugin not found*.
</div>
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-alert"></i>&nbsp; Real case — mosaicatcher</h4>

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em;"}
**Sequential checkpoints** — *e.g.* `mosaic_count → summarise_ploidy → filter_bad_cells` — exercise the DAG-reevaluation path harder than most pipelines.
:::

<div style="margin-top: 0.4em; padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #fef5e7; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<b>v8</b> — never reached a working state for our chained checkpoints (DAG re-eval bug on the second checkpoint).<br/>
<b>v9</b> — works · but **some 9.x point releases** silently regress on the same DAG (e.g. group jobs + checkpoint interactions) → we pin a known-good range.
</div>

<div style="margin-top: 0.4em; padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #f4ecf7; border-left: 4px solid #8E44AD; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-lightbulb-on" style="color: #8E44AD;"></i>&nbsp; **Lesson:** treat the engine like a dependency — pin `snakemake==9.X.Y`, pin **every plugin**, gate upgrades on the full test matrix.
</div>
:::
:::

## What we tune on the cluster

<div class="pillars-table">
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-cached pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Workflow caching</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">SNAKEMAKE_OUTPUT_CACHE</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-cube-outline pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Container caching</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">apptainer-prefix</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-database pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Storage staging</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">fs plugin · scratch</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-group pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Grouping &amp; arrays</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">group · slurm-array-jobs</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-package-variant pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">EESSI / env-mods</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">--sdm env-modules</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-chart-line pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Job optimisation</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">slurm-efficiency-report</code></div>
</div>

## 1 · Caching — workflow + containers

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22;"><i class="mdi mdi-cached"></i>&nbsp; Workflow output cache</h4>

```bash
export SNAKEMAKE_OUTPUT_CACHE=\
  /scratch_cached/<group>/snakemake_cache
```

Per rule:
```{.snakemake}
rule index_ref:
    output: "ref.fa.bwt"
    cache: True   # → goes into $SNAKEMAKE_OUTPUT_CACHE
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em;"}
The hash key includes **input file content, rule code, params, software-env, version**. As long as the recipe is identical, **user B reuses what user A built** — even from a different working tree.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.74em; margin-top: 0.3em; color: #7f8c8d;"}
Concretely: BWA index on hg38 ≈ 1 h CPU · STAR index ≈ 1.5 h · gnomAD VCF tabix ≈ 30 min. Build once per group, not once per user.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22;"><i class="mdi mdi-cube-outline"></i>&nbsp; Container cache</h4>

```yaml
# profile
apptainer-prefix: /scratch_cached/<group>/apptainer
```

<i class="mdi mdi-folder-lock" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; On `/scratch_cached` (same fast tier as the workflow cache) → image pulled **once** for the whole group.

<i class="mdi mdi-rocket" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Pre-pull manually: `apptainer pull --dir $APPTAINER_CACHEDIR docker://...` (no Snakemake "container-prewarm" flag exists — first job pulls).

<div style="margin-top: 0.5em; padding: 0.5em 0.8em; background: #fdebd0; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-package-variant" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; **Skip the cache entirely** when **EESSI** covers the tool — `envmodules:` loads from CernVM-FS, no image pull, no conda solve.
</div>
:::
:::

## 2 · Storage — what the `fs` plugin actually does

::: {style="font-size: 0.86em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
The `fs` storage plugin treats **a local filesystem path as a "remote" storage backend**. Snakemake **stages inputs in** to a fast per-job location before the job runs, then **stages outputs back** when it finishes — same code path as S3/GCS storage plugins, but the "remote" is just another POSIX mount.
:::

::: {.threestep}
<span class="threestep-box">shared FS (slow)</span>
<span class="threestep-arrow">→ stage-in →</span>
<span class="threestep-box">local scratch (fast)</span>
<span class="threestep-arrow">→ run →</span>
<span class="threestep-box">stage-out</span>
<span class="threestep-arrow">→</span>
<span class="threestep-box">shared FS</span>
:::

::: {.columns style="margin-top: 0.5em;"}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{.yaml filename="profile/config.yaml"}
executor: slurm
default-storage-provider: fs              # use fs as backend
local-storage-prefix: /scratch/$USER/wf   # per-job staging dir
remote-job-local-storage-prefix: /tmp/$USER/wf

shared-fs-usage:           # what stays on shared FS, not staged
  - persistence            # .snakemake/ metadata
  - software-deployment    # conda/apptainer
  - sources                # the Snakefile itself
  # input-output absent → staged through fs plugin
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {style="font-size: 0.82em;"}
**Why bother**

- Compute nodes hammer **local NVMe**, not the shared parallel FS — no metadata storms.
- Same plugin contract as `s3` / `gcs` → swap backends without changing rules.
- Inputs are **copied**, not symlinked → safe with `temp()` cleanup.

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em; margin-top: 0.4em; color: #7f8c8d;"}
CLI: `--default-storage-provider` · `--local-storage-prefix` · `--shared-fs-usage` · [`plugins/storage/fs`](https://snakemake.github.io/snakemake-plugin-catalog/plugins/storage/fs.html)
:::
:::
:::
:::

## 3 · Job grouping — map · sort · dedup · index → one job

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{.snakemake}
rule bwa:
    input:  "fq/{s}.fq.gz"
    output: temp("bam/{s}.sort.bam")
    group:  "alignment_per_cell"

rule sort:
    input:  "bam/{s}.sort.bam"
    output: temp("bam/{s}.sorted.bam")
    group:  "alignment_per_cell"

rule dedup:
    input:  "bam/{s}.sorted.bam"
    output: temp("bam/{s}.dedup.bam")
    group:  "alignment_per_cell"

rule index:
    input:  "bam/{s}.dedup.bam"
    output: "bam/{s}.bam.bai"
    group:  "alignment_per_cell"
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<div class="slurm-viz">
<div class="slurm-header"><i class="mdi mdi-server-network"></i>&nbsp; <b>1 SLURM job per sample</b></div>
<div class="slurm-step">bwa mem</div>
<div class="slurm-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="slurm-step">samtools sort</div>
<div class="slurm-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="slurm-step">mark_duplicates</div>
<div class="slurm-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="slurm-step">samtools index</div>
</div>

::: {style="margin-top: 0.7em; font-size: 0.78em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-lightbulb-on" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Shared scratch · zero stage-in between steps · `temp()` cleaned at group end
:::

<div style="margin-top: 0.5em; padding: 0.5em 0.8em; background: #fdebd0; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.74em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-alert" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; **Specs are aligned at the group, not the rule.** Pick the *most demanding* rule's resources (cpu, mem, constraint=milan) — the whole group inherits them via `set-resources` on the group name.
</div>
:::
:::

## 4 · Job arrays — pack 1-CPU tasks into one SLURM submission

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{.yaml filename="profile/config.yaml"}
executor: slurm
slurm-array-jobs: all       # all eligible rules
slurm-array-limit: 1000     # tasks / array

# pack 10 single-CPU jobs into one array
group-components:
  - count_cell=10
```

For a per-cell rule that needs **1 CPU each**:

```{.snakemake}
rule count_cell:
    input:  "bam/{cell}.bam"
    output: "counts/{cell}.tsv"
    threads: 1
    group:   "count_cell"     # ← the array
```

What lands on SLURM:

```bash
$ squeue -u $USER
JOBID         NAME       NCPUS  ST
12345_[1-10]  count_cell    1   PD
# 1 sbatch · 10 tasks · 1 cpu each
# SLURM sees a 10-cpu allocation
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<div class="slurm-viz">
<div class="slurm-header"><i class="mdi mdi-server-network"></i>&nbsp; <b>1 sbatch · 10 array tasks · 10 cpus total</b></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">task 1</span><span class="array-step">1 cpu · cell A</span></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">task 2</span><span class="array-step">1 cpu · cell B</span></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">task 3</span><span class="array-step">1 cpu · cell C</span></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">…</span><span class="array-step">…</span></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">task 10</span><span class="array-step">1 cpu · cell J</span></div>
</div>

::: {style="margin-top: 0.6em; font-size: 0.76em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-lightbulb-on" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; *In theory:* big win for **many short 1-CPU jobs** (per-cell QC, per-chrom split) — one scheduler decision instead of N.
:::

<div style="margin-top: 0.4em; padding: 0.5em 0.8em; background: #fdecea; border-left: 4px solid #C0392B; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.76em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-alert-octagon" style="color: #C0392B;"></i>&nbsp; **In practice (our setup): parallelism is lost.** The 10 tasks inside the group ran **sequentially** in the same allocation — same wallclock as N separate jobs, no speed-up. Test on your cluster.
</div>

<div style="margin-top: 0.3em; font-size: 0.74em; color: #7f8c8d;">
<i class="mdi mdi-alert" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Heterogeneous resources → don't mix into one array.
</div>
:::
:::

## 5 · EESSI — env-modules with native optimisation

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em; text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
**EESSI** = European Environment for Scientific Software Installations — a **CernVM-FS** stream of EasyBuild-compiled scientific software, **dispatched per microarchitecture** (`zen3`, `icelake`, `haswell` …), mountable on any HPC.
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin: 0 0 0.3em; text-align: center;">Bootstrap once</h4>

```bash
source /cvmfs/software.eessi.io/versions/2023.06/init/bash
module load BWA SAMtools STAR
```

<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin: 0.8em 0 0.3em; text-align: center;">Use per rule</h4>

```{.snakemake}
rule align:
    envmodules: "BWA/0.7.17", "SAMtools/1.18"
    shell: "bwa mem ... | samtools sort ..."
```

```bash
snakemake --sdm env-modules ...
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<div style="background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fdebd0 0%, #fef5e7 100%); border: 1.5px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 10px; padding: 0.9em 1em;">

<div style="font-size: 0.85em; margin: 0.2em 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-rocket-launch" style="color: #b9620a;"></i>&nbsp; <b>Fast</b> — no conda solve, no image pull · first job runs immediately</div>

<div style="font-size: 0.85em; margin: 0.45em 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-chip" style="color: #b9620a;"></i>&nbsp; <b>Optimised</b> — CPU-tuned binaries → wallclock wins on AVX-heavy tools</div>

<div style="font-size: 0.85em; margin: 0.45em 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-earth" style="color: #b9620a;"></i>&nbsp; <b>Portable</b> — identical versions across any HPC mounting `/cvmfs`</div>

<div style="font-size: 0.85em; margin: 0.45em 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-shield-check" style="color: #b9620a;"></i>&nbsp; <b>Reproducible</b> — comparable to containers, no I/O overhead</div>

<div style="font-size: 0.85em; margin: 0.45em 0 0.2em;"><i class="mdi mdi-cash-multiple" style="color: #b9620a;"></i>&nbsp; <b>Cheap</b> — zero per-user env duplication → group quota saved</div>

</div>

::: {style="font-size: 0.72em; margin-top: 0.4em; color: #7f8c8d; text-align: center;"}
[eessi.io](https://www.eessi.io)
:::
:::
:::

## 6 · Job optimisation — efficiency report

::: {style="font-size: 0.92em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
The SLURM executor emits a **per-rule CPU & memory utilisation report** at the end of each run — read it to right-size `set-resources:` (rules that ask for 32 GB but use 2 GB, or run at 20% CPU).
:::

```{.yaml filename="profile/config.yaml"}
slurm-efficiency-report:       true
slurm-efficiency-report-path:  efficiency.txt
slurm-efficiency-threshold:    0.8        # flag rules below 80%
```

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
<span class="flow-strip">
<span class="flow-box">run</span>
<span class="flow-arrow">→</span>
<span class="flow-box">efficiency report</span>
<span class="flow-arrow">→</span>
<span class="flow-box">tune set-resources</span>
<span class="flow-arrow">→</span>
<span class="flow-box">cheaper next run</span>
</span>
:::


## Bonus · dependency cooldowns

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-shield-lock" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Tell your resolver to **ignore anything newer than N days** — malicious releases are usually yanked within hours.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em; margin-bottom: 0.5em; color: #6e3906; background: #fdebd0; padding: 0.5em 0.8em; border-left: 3px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px;"}
**Mini Shai-Hulud wave, Apr–May 2026** — a self-propagating worm hit **PyTorch-Lightning** (PyPI, ~42 min live) and **TanStack** (42 packages / 84 versions, [CVE-2026-45321](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45321)) — combined ~10 M downloads/mo. **A 7-day cooldown blocks both.**
:::

::: {.columns style="margin-top: 0.4em;"}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin: 0 0 0.4em;"><i class="mdi mdi-language-python"></i>&nbsp; pip 26.1 *(Apr 2026)*</h4>

```{.bash}
pip install \
  --uploaded-prior-to=P7D \
  requests
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
- 26.0 → absolute date · 26.1 → relative
- Also configurable in `pip.conf`
- Uses PEP 700 upload-time data
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin: 0 0 0.4em;"><i class="mdi mdi-package-variant"></i>&nbsp; Pixi · `exclude-newer`</h4>

```{.toml}
[workspace]
exclude-newer = "14d"

[exclude-newer]
openssl = "0d"
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
- Per-channel & per-package overrides
- Same concept as uv / rattler
:::
:::
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em; margin-top: 0.6em; color: #7f8c8d; text-align: center;"}
7 days is the commonly cited default · [Richard Si — *What's new in pip 26.1*](https://ichard26.github.io/blog/2026/04/whats-new-in-pip-26.1/)
:::

## Dataflow paradigm — pull vs push {visibility="uncounted"}

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
<span class="flow-strip">
<span class="flow-box">fq/{s}.fq.gz</span>
<span class="flow-arrow">— align →</span>
<span class="flow-box">bam/{s}.bam</span>
<span class="flow-arrow">— call →</span>
<span class="flow-box">vcf/cohort.vcf</span>
</span>
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h3 style="color: #1F3A5F; margin: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-arrow-up-bold-circle"></i>&nbsp; Snakemake — **pull**</h3>

> Start from the **target file**, walk back to inputs.

```{.snakemake style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
rule all:
    input: "vcf/cohort.vcf"   # ◀ the target

rule call:
    input:  "bam/{s}.bam"
    output: "vcf/{s}.vcf"

rule align:
    input:  "fq/{s}.fq.gz"    # ◀ leaf
    output: "bam/{s}.bam"
```

```bash
snakemake vcf/cohort.vcf --cores 8
```
Static DAG, resolved before anything runs.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h3 style="color: #1F3A5F; margin: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-arrow-down-bold-circle"></i>&nbsp; Nextflow — **push**</h3>

> Start from the **source channel**, flow forward.

```{.groovy style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
workflow {
  reads = Channel.fromFilePairs(
    'fq/*_{1,2}.fq.gz'        // ◀ the source
  )
  ALIGN(reads) | CALL | view
}

process ALIGN { /* fq → bam */ }
process CALL  { /* bam → vcf */ }
```

```bash
nextflow run main.nf -resume
```
Dynamic DAG, materialised as channels emit.
:::
:::

## Resume / cache — what actually invalidates {visibility="uncounted"}

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 0.95em; color: #1F3A5F; margin-bottom: 0.5em; font-weight: 500;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-help-circle" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; *"My input / code / container changed. Will the job rerun?"*
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.rerun-card .rerun-smk}
<h4><i class="mdi mdi-snake"></i>&nbsp; Snakemake — `--rerun-triggers`</h4>

| Signal | Default |
|---|---|
| `mtime` of inputs | ✅ |
| `input` set (paths) | ✅ |
| `params` value | ✅ |
| `code` of rule body | ✅ |
| `software-env` hash | ✅ |

::: {style="font-size: 0.74em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
Each trigger is **named & opt-out-able**: `--rerun-triggers mtime params input`.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.72em; margin-top: 0.4em; padding: 0.4em 0.6em; background: #fdecea; border-left: 3px solid #C0392B; border-radius: 4px;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-alert" style="color: #C0392B;"></i>&nbsp; **Sensitive in dev.** Touching `code` / `params` during iteration reruns every downstream job — pin `--rerun-triggers mtime` while iterating.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.rerun-card .rerun-nf}
<h4><i class="mdi mdi-source-branch"></i>&nbsp; Nextflow `-resume`</h4>

| Signal | Default | `cache 'deep'` |
|---|---|---|
| path + size + mtime | ✅ | path+size |
| file SHA-256 | — | ✅ |
| `script:` body | ✅ | ✅ |
| `container:` ID | ✅ | ✅ |
| `ext` directive | ✅ | ✅ |
| other directives | ❌ * | ❌ * |

::: {style="font-size: 0.72em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
* unless referenced in `script:` body via `${task.…}`. NF hashes code, container & ext; *"all content-hashed"* still false — file content needs `cache 'deep'`.
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {style="margin-top: 0.5em; padding: 0.45em 0.9em; background: #fef5e7; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-information"></i>&nbsp; **Bottom line.** Default invalidation surfaces are comparable. Differences: Snakemake exposes each trigger by **name** for opt-out; Nextflow re-hashes if any *referenced* directive value moves; **file content** needs `cache 'deep'` (NF) or explicit `--rerun-triggers mtime` opt-out (SMK).
:::

## Distribution layer {visibility="uncounted"}

| <i class="mdi mdi-format-list-checks" style="color: #1F3A5F;"></i>&nbsp; Capability | <i class="mdi mdi-snake" style="color: #208F6E;"></i> Snakemake | <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/logos/master/nf-core-logos/nf-core-logo-square.svg" style="height: 18px; vertical-align: middle;"/>&nbsp; Nextflow / nf-core |
|---|---|---|
| <i class="mdi mdi-tag-multiple"></i>&nbsp; Per-rule env | `conda:` + `container:` + **`envmodules:`** | `conda` + `container` directive |
| <i class="mdi mdi-layers-triple"></i>&nbsp; Compose | `--sdm conda apptainer env-modules` | engine + conda |
| <i class="mdi mdi-cpu-64-bit"></i>&nbsp; HPC env-modules / EESSI | native via `envmodules:` | native via `module:` directive |
| <i class="mdi mdi-warehouse"></i>&nbsp; Curated registry | snakemake-wrappers | BioContainers · mulled · **Seqera Containers** |
| <i class="mdi mdi-hammer-wrench"></i>&nbsp; Build on demand | — | **Wave** |
| <i class="mdi mdi-folder-network"></i>&nbsp; POSIX over object storage | — | **Fusion** |

::: {.columns style="margin-top: 0.4em;"}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<div style="padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #e8f1f8; border-left: 4px solid #2980B9; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<b>Wave</b> — Seqera's container-provisioning service. Takes a conda spec attached to a process, **builds an OCI container on demand** with that environment, caches it in a registry. Supports `amd64` + `arm64`. **Apache-2.0, open source.**
</div>
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
<div style="padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #fef5e7; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<b>Fusion</b> — a virtual **POSIX layer** that lets processes read/write S3, GCS or Azure Blob as if they were a mounted directory. Avoids stage-in/stage-out copies on cloud. **Commercial**, part of Seqera Platform.
</div>
:::
:::

## When does each fit? {visibility="uncounted"}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #1F3A5F;"><i class="mdi mdi-snake"></i>&nbsp; Snakemake fits when…</h4>

- Team is <i class="mdi mdi-language-python"></i> Python-native
- Pipeline is **file / target-driven**
- You want the **DAG up-front**
- Debugging needs interactive Python
- One Snakefile, readable end-to-end
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #1F3A5F;"><i class="mdi mdi-source-branch"></i>&nbsp; Nextflow fits when…</h4>

- Team has Groovy / JVM people
- Pipeline is **stream / event-driven**
- **AWS Batch** or **Fusion** matter
- You want **nf-core** off-the-shelf
- You want **Seqera Platform** observability
:::
:::
